id: A Christmas Cracker-Waitangi Park, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: A Christmas Cracker
long_description:
Gather the elves in your family and head to Waitangi Park for a free day of festive fun. A Christmas Cracker provides a host of yuletide entertainment and activities for the whole whānau. There’ll be ice skating, face painting, caricatures, Christmas crafts and a foam pit. Roving performers, magicians and Christmas mascots will also add to the party atmosphere. The live entertainment includes dance groups, choirs, brass bands, a ukulele group, singers, and even a bit of pantomime.

If you run out of energy food trucks will be on site so you can grab something to eat. Before you leave, remind the littlest elves to post their wish list in Santa’s Mailbox.

id: Queen: It’s a Kinda magic-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Queen: It’s a Kinda magic
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
The beloved rock anthem ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’ turned 50 in 2025. To celebrate the anniversary of British band Queen’s famous song and many others, a tribute act is touring and stopping in Wellington. The Opera House will pulsate to ‘Queen: It’s a Kinda Magic’. The show will celebrate the legacy of Queen and its front man Freddy Mercury. Think big sound, big screens, crazy lighting, and outlandish costumes. This is a real rock experience with all the bells and whistles. 

Dominic Warren will front the performance taking lead vocals, guitar and piano. All songs are in Freddie’s original key. He’s also got the wit, charm, and bravado to pull off an homage to the ultimate rock vocalist. Get ready to mosh to We Will Rock You, We Are the Champions, and Radio GaGa. You’ll also hear I Want to Break Free, Somebody to Love, Don’t Stop Me Now, Another One Bites the Dust, A Kind of Magic, and of course, Bohemian Rhapsody.

id: Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra-Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall-Wellington NZ
name: Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra
venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
long_description:
In what could be described as a ‘uke fluke’ one of the city’s greatest homegrown bands is reforming. After a ten-year hiatus the Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra (WIUO) is back and will perform at the newly reopened Wellington Town Hall.

The spectacular venue played an important role in the orchestra's story since its earliest days so WIUO is thrilled to present the concert there. The performance will feature beloved classics, new material and, inevitably, a few trademark surprises.

Fans already know that WIUO’s gloriously eclectic repertoire moves effortlessly between pop hits, rock classics, country ballads, waiata Māori, Pacific music, indie favourites and unexpected deep cuts. Attendees at the March 2027 gig can also expect spontaneous comedy and plenty of audience participation.

The Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra was founded in 2005 by friends Age Pryor and Bret McKenzie, what began as an informal gathering of ukulele enthusiasts at Wellington's Deluxe Café quickly evolved into one of New Zealand's most celebrated live acts. Over the following decade WIUO captivated audiences across Aotearoa, Australia, the United States, China and Japan. It released four bestselling EPs and an album, collaborating with internationally renowned artists, and inspiring thousands of people to discover the joy of making music.

id: Teeks — Lovers Comet-Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall-Wellington NZ
name: Teeks — Lovers Comet
venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
long_description:
Drawing from his highly anticipated new album ‘Lovers Comet’ the concert sees the artist enter a new creative orbit. Following a period of profound personal and creative evolution, the album delves into desire, intimacy, identity and the transformative power of love. The album and concert promises to invite listeners to confront their own gravitational pulls. What draws them in, what breaks them open, and what sets them free.

Teeks says of the music “…it explores love not as fantasy, but as a cosmic phenomenon: magnetic, unpredictable, breathtaking, and occasionally destructive.” Join one of New Zealand’s most exciting soul voices on a journey as observer, narrator, and lover caught in orbit.

id: Beth Orton-Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall-Wellington NZ
name: Beth Orton
venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
long_description:
English singer-songwriter Beth Orton is one of the best-known practitioners of folktronica. This is a subgenre where folk songs are set to electronic beats. This unique sound, popularised in the late ‘90s and early ‘00s, can be heard when Beth travels to Wellington in March. Her tour takes her to Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall where audiences will get to hear intimate and adventurous song writing. 

Beth has released nine studio albums including the most recent ‘The Ground Above’ (2026). Thirty years into her career she is still evolving as an artist. Music blog Pitchfork proclaimed, “Orton is one of the UK singer-songwriters of her generation working at the highest level right now.” Collaborations with the likes of Andrew Weatherall, William Orbit, and The Chemical Brothers indicates he is not just your average singer-songwriter.
